subject: science
title: KS3 / Year 7-9 Science - Biology Environment Reading
subtitle: Reading passages for KS3 biology environment revision.
description: Five KS3 reading passages with fact retrieval, inference and explanation questions. The passages cover ecosystems, pollution, climate change, the carbon cycle, conservation and sustainability.

data.sourcePassage: An environment is made from the living and non-living things around an organism. In a pond, the living parts include algae, pondweed, insects, fish and decomposers. The non-living parts include water, mud, light, oxygen and temperature. These parts form an ecosystem because organisms interact with each other and with the physical environment. Plants make food by photosynthesis, herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat other animals, and decomposers break down dead material. If insect numbers fall after pesticide use, birds may have less food. The final effect is hard to predict because ecosystems have many links. High biodiversity usually makes an ecosystem more stable because several species may perform similar roles.

questions.question: What is an environment?
questions.modelAnswer: The living and non-living surroundings of an organism.

questions.question: Which item from the passage is non-living?
questions.modelAnswer: Water

questions.question: Why might pesticide use affect birds?
questions.modelAnswer: If pesticide reduces insect numbers, birds that feed on insects may have less food.

questions.question: Why are ecosystem effects not always simple?
questions.modelAnswer: Ecosystems contain many linked organisms and physical factors, so a change in one part can affect several others.

questions.question: Explain why high biodiversity can make an ecosystem more stable.
questions.modelAnswer: If one species decreases, another species may fill a similar role, so the ecosystem is less likely to collapse after one change.

data.sourcePassage: Fertilisers help crops grow because they contain mineral ions such as nitrates. If too much fertiliser is used, rain can wash it from fields into streams, rivers or ponds. Extra nitrates can cause algae to grow quickly. This may block light from aquatic plants. When algae and plants die, decomposers break them down and use oxygen from the water. Fish and small invertebrates may decrease if dissolved oxygen becomes too low. Some pollutants can also bioaccumulate. A tiny amount of pollutant in a small organism may seem low, but a predator eats many prey. This can make pollutant concentration higher further along a food chain, so a bird of prey may be most affected.

questions.question: Which mineral ions in fertilisers are named in the passage?
questions.modelAnswer: Nitrates.

questions.question: What can wash fertiliser from fields into rivers?
questions.modelAnswer: Heavy rain

questions.question: Explain why fish may die after rapid algae growth.
questions.modelAnswer: Dead algae are decomposed, and decomposers use oxygen from the water, so dissolved oxygen falls and fish may not have enough for respiration.

questions.question: Why can a predator have more pollutant than one prey organism?
questions.modelAnswer: A predator eats many prey, so pollutant from several prey builds up in its body.

questions.question: Suggest one farming action that could reduce fertiliser run-off.
questions.modelAnswer: Use fertiliser more carefully, add buffer strips or hedgerows, and avoid spreading fertiliser before heavy rain.

data.sourcePassage: Weather is the short-term condition of the atmosphere, such as today's rain, wind or temperature. Climate is the long-term pattern of weather in a region, measured over many years. One cold day does not disprove global warming because one day is weather, not climate. The natural greenhouse effect is needed for life. Sunlight reaches Earth, the surface warms, and Earth gives out infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour absorb some outgoing infrared radiation and return some heat towards Earth. Human activities, especially burning fossil fuels and deforestation, increase greenhouse gas concentrations. This enhanced greenhouse effect causes average global temperature to rise and can change rainfall, sea level, heatwaves, habitats and crop growth.

questions.question: What is weather?
questions.modelAnswer: Short-term atmospheric conditions such as rain, wind or temperature.

questions.question: Which gas listed is a greenhouse gas?
questions.modelAnswer: Methane

questions.question: Why does one cold day not disprove global warming?
questions.modelAnswer: One cold day is weather, while global warming is a long-term rise in average temperature shown by many records over time.

questions.question: What do greenhouse gases do to outgoing infrared radiation?
questions.modelAnswer: They absorb some outgoing infrared radiation and return some heat towards Earth.

questions.question: Explain the difference between the natural and enhanced greenhouse effect.
questions.modelAnswer: The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life. The enhanced greenhouse effect is extra warming caused by increased greenhouse gases from human activity.

data.sourcePassage: Carbon is stored in the atmosphere, organisms, soil, oceans, rocks and fossil fuels. In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air as plants and algae make glucose. Feeding moves carbon compounds from plants to animals. Respiration by plants, animals and microorganisms releases carbon dioxide. Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste, returning carbon to soil and often carbon dioxide to the air. Combustion of coal, oil, gas or wood releases carbon dioxide quickly. Deforestation changes the carbon cycle because fewer trees are left to photosynthesise. If trees are burned or left to decay, stored carbon is released. Deforestation also causes habitat loss, reduces biodiversity, increases soil erosion and can disrupt food chains.

questions.question: Name one carbon store from the passage.
questions.modelAnswer: The atmosphere, organisms, soil, oceans, rocks or fossil fuels.

questions.question: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air?
questions.modelAnswer: Photosynthesis

questions.question: How does feeding move carbon?
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon compounds pass from one organism to another when animals eat plants or other animals.

questions.question: Why can burning fossil fuels change the carbon cycle?
questions.modelAnswer: It releases carbon dioxide quickly from long-term fossil fuel stores into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Explain two ways deforestation can increase atmospheric carbon dioxide.
questions.modelAnswer: There are fewer trees to remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis, and carbon stored in trees can be released if wood is burned or decomposes.

data.sourcePassage: Sustainability means using resources in a way that meets current needs without making life harder for future generations. Conservation means protecting species, habitats and ecosystems. A council choosing how to manage land beside a river should consider environmental, social and economic evidence. A nature reserve may improve biodiversity, protect habitats and reduce flooding, but it costs money to manage. Housing may provide homes and jobs, but it can cause habitat loss and more surface run-off. A mixed-use plan may keep some habitat while also building some homes, but it still needs careful management. Good environmental decisions use data, such as species counts, flood records, traffic counts, air quality readings or waste audits, and they recognise limitations instead of overclaiming.

questions.question: What does sustainability mean?
questions.modelAnswer: Using resources to meet current needs without making life harder for future generations.

questions.question: Which option may improve biodiversity beside a river?
questions.modelAnswer: A nature reserve

questions.question: Give one environmental limitation of housing beside a river.
questions.modelAnswer: It may cause habitat loss and more surface run-off.

questions.question: Why should decisions use evidence such as species counts or flood records?
questions.modelAnswer: Evidence helps judge whether a solution works and prevents unsupported claims.

questions.question: Why might a mixed-use plan be a compromise?
questions.modelAnswer: It can provide some homes and green space while keeping part of the habitat, but it still has management costs and some environmental impact.
